summary.intent: Implement ADR 13 (interrupted `version` runs resume from a checkpoint ref) end to end in an agentic fashion, after the user approved the ADR and asked to skip human ceremony. Also decide whether the other ADRs needed fixing.
summary.outcome: Added checkpoint primitives in the model layer, resume/refuse logic in the graph and CLI `version` handler, new errors E340/E341, a real-binary differential test suite (4 tests), and the docs, spec, ADR enforcement section and changeset. Everything was committed locally with a signature and doc-check passed; the PR was not yet opened, and the ADR 12 cleanup was proposed but not started.

repo: ADRs 1-11 have full structure (decision, rejected options, enforcement, revisit, sources) and are historical records; changed decisions get a new ADR rather than a rewrite. ADR 12 alone lacks Enforcement and Revisit sections and bundles behaviour that belongs in specs.
Per the docs README, behaviour goes in `docs/specs/*.json`, architecture placement in `docs/architecture/*.md`, and ADR Enforcement is filled in by the implementing PR naming real tests.
Error codes: E340 and E341 were free. `crates/callisto-graph/tests/error_registry_architecture.rs` only checks that codes appear in `docs/errors.md`, so new rows must be added there.
`testing/check-comments.sh` rejects history-narration words such as 'now' in comments, and clippy (`-D warnings`) flags complex tuple types in tests, which are fixed with a type alias like `Shape`.
The `CommandRunner` trait in `callisto-model/src/exec.rs` gained `run_with_env` (fail-closed default) so a checkpoint can use a temporary index via an env var; the CLI runner implements it.
`lower_hex` in `release/digest.rs` was widened to `pub(crate)` and reused instead of duplicated.

Existing tests (`partial_run_tests`, `pre_mode_tests`) asserted the old fail-closed retry behaviour, so they were renamed and rewritten to expect that a retry finishes the run (e.g. `..._is_finished_by_a_retry`).
Handler ordering matters: plan first, then the E121 partial-run check when no checkpoint exists, to preserve earlier error precedence.

code.finding: New module for checkpoint create/read/delete and a detached worktree of the checkpoint, never touching the user's index or working tree.

Differential tests with the real binary; root-case paths must be "" not "." because `create_dir_all` fails on a trailing `/.`. Disabling checkpoint creation made them fail, confirming they catch the bug.
Adds `checkpoint_input_changes` and `checkpoint_abort_commands`, re-exported from `commands/mod.rs`, implementing the input-changed refusal (E340) and abort guidance.

workflow: Verify that new tests detect the bug by temporarily disabling the fix and confirming they fail.
Run the project check script (`check3.sh`) and then `just lint`, clippy and the full workspace test suite, since failures in unrelated tests can reveal behaviour changes.
Keep ADRs short: decision, rejected options, consequences, revisit trigger and sources. Move explanation to specs and architecture docs.

friction: Earlier ADR 13 drafts were too long because they explained reasoning instead of stating the decision.
The first check run failed on comment-checker and clippy violations, which required fixes.
The full test suite failed on three existing tests that encoded the old retry-refusal behaviour, requiring investigation and rewrites.
A sed command using `\n` in a pattern for a multi-line edit was a no-op and had to be redone with an Edit.
The test harness's `"."` root path broke `create_dir_all`, requiring sed normalisation.
open_items: Open the PR for `feat/version-checkpoint-resume`; the commit is local and nothing has been pushed.
ADR 12 cleanup: add Enforcement and Revisit sections, and reduce behaviour bullets to spec pointers in a separate small docs PR (proposed, awaiting the user's go-ahead).
The wire-compat table update lists the checkpoint ref; this should be confirmed in review.
A test was skipped in the workspace run (`a_version_the_registry_serves_is_exact`), so its status should be checked separately.
